preamble: Solve the clues and fit them into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: Italian road divisions, last of same

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords
a road is divided into lanes

indicators.note: 'last of' tells us to keep only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: final letter of 'same'

explanation.surface: Someone describing how Italian roads are marked out into lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: MI is the crossword spelling of the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Milanese describes a person or thing from Milan, so it can stand for an Italian adjective or native.

clue.text: See 10
Trouble with organ: nothing is in code
Once more say "Well read student won't appear"

indicators.note: something that won't appear is missing, so that element is dropped from the word

parts.note: able to read and educated
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A teacher repeats a remark that the bookish pupil is absent today.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from LITERATE to leave ITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat or restate something, doing or saying it again.

clue.text: Such deviation: slab in floor unlined

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective-like noun that qualifies 'deviation' in the statistical phrase

indicators.note: 'unlined' asks us to take a line away, and in crosswords a line is a railway

parts.note: a quarry tile is an unglazed floor tile
RY, railway, is the line removed

explanation.surface: A builder notes that one paving slab sits unevenly, missing its lining.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop RY from QUARRY TILE. Quartile deviation is a statistical measure of spread, half the interquartile range.
explanation.definitionFit: Statisticians speak of the quartile deviation, a measure of how widely data are spread.

clue.text: What makes B A? Extended small abode?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the musical sign that lowers a note two semitones
second meaning: a small apartment made twice as big

explanation.walkthrough: B lowered by two semitones sounds as A. A flat is a British apartment, so doubling one extends it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation, this sign drops a note by a whole tone; jokily it also describes an apartment knocked through into two.

clue.text: Look hard and see inside: give nought to eat

indicators.note: 'inside' places one element within the other

parts.note: to gaze fixedly
V is short for Latin vide, see

explanation.surface: Instructions to peer into a cupboard and find there is nothing to feed anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from vide, as in cross-references.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone is to deprive them of food entirely.

clue.text: Destructive type left one in this display

indicators.note: a display arranges things for show, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vandal has left one item in this exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all values and institutions, sometimes favouring their destruction.

clue.text: Beneath the waves it goes about distressed

indicators.note: distressed means battered and knocked out of shape, so the word is disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vessel under the sea moves around in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German submarine, a vessel that travels under the sea's surface.

clue.text: Ungainly mob takes fish when good's the sport

parts.note: a gang is a crowd or band
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
a second route: G for good joined to the sport of fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A clumsy crowd goes fishing when the sport is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail is a second route: G for good plus ANGLING, the sport, also spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling means tall, thin and awkward in movement, a near synonym for ungainly.

clue.text: With cranesbill poet George keeps sibling short

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one element goes inside the other

parts.note: George Herbert, the 17th-century English religious poet
brother cut short

explanation.surface: A poet keeps his brother's flowers close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet George' points to the metaphysical poet George Herbert, whose surname is the outer part.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Robert is a common wild geranium, and cranesbill is the general name for that genus of plants.

clue.text: Protector or practitioner of game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a guardian or custodian
second meaning: a goalkeeper or wicketkeeper, or one who keeps game birds

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone guards a thing or simply plays at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper guards things, and in sport a goalkeeper or gamekeeper is a specialist role.

clue.text: Choice pole for fishing, capital for shrew: shortage of fuel for aircraft centre too

parts.note: a pet project is a favoured choice
a fishing rod
the capital of Italy

parts.words: shortage of fuel for aircraft centre too
parts.note: a second route: petrol cut short, then the drome of an aerodrome

explanation.surface: A rambling list of fishing gear, a capital city, and an airport running out of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The last part offers PETRO (petrol, short) plus DROME, an airfield, as a second route to the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrodromus is a genus of elephant shrew, and the anglicised name refers to that small long-snouted mammal.

clue.text: Spruce tree destroyed by something with three feet

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the word is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: spruce and trim both mean neat
the word tree rearranged

explanation.surface: A spruce tree is felled by a three-legged creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce tree' reads as one conifer; spruce is the adjective neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimeter is a line of verse made of three metrical units, or feet.

clue.text: For all that strayed the Sabbath was designed

indicators.note: something designed is planned and arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher's line that the holy day was made even for those who went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest kept by religious tradition.

clue.text: (A near mad answer) Folk from desert climes

indicators.note: 'near' means almost, so the word falls just short of its end

parts.note: taken as written
rabid means raving or frenzied
standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside about a crazy reply, then a note on desert peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: RABID loses its last letter to give RABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabians are natives of Arabia, a peninsula known for its desert climate.

clue.text: Bleak House campaigner has explosive near

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite
by means beside or close to

explanation.surface: A Dickens activist has a bomb close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Jellyby in Dickens's Bleak House neglects her family to campaign for an African mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Jellyby is the obsessive philanthropic campaigner in Dickens's novel Bleak House.

clue.text: Some weapons' parts in bags with witch's rhymes
Where law is turned to ass, a Francophone

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a loon is a fool, as is an ass

explanation.surface: Echoes Mr Bumble's line that the law is an ass, set in a French-speaking country.
explanation.definitionFit: Walloons are the French-speaking people of southern Belgium.

clue.text: Arches in skull with right make Mozart gay

indicators.note: gay in its old sense of merry and lively, so the letters frolic into a new order
the answer plus a right would make the phrase, so a right must be removed from it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Absurd: bones of the skull turning a composer cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Add R to the answer and you have the letters of MOZART GAY; so remove R from those letters and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The zygomata are the cheekbone arches, bony bridges on each side of the skull.

clue.text: You've swallowed broken pipe, I'm glad to say

indicators.note: broken means shattered, so the word's letters are scattered and reassembled
to have swallowed something is to hold it within, so one element goes inside the other

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
pipe rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark to someone who has swallowed a broken pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the archaic form of you, still heard in dialect and in phrases like 'hear ye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yippee is an exclamation of delight, so it is what one says when glad.

clue.text: See 22
New Forest opera singer took in kid

definitions.note: describes the person by what they did; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the following word appears in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: forest rearranged
a father is a standard singing role in opera, as in Humperdinck's Hansel and Gretel

explanation.surface: A singer from an opera company based in the New Forest adopts a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a woodland area in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A foster father is a man who raises a child not his own, having taken it into his home.

clue.text: These subatomic things on page unknown

definitions.text: These subatomic things on page unknown

indicators.note: in this reading 'on' means placed after, so the word before it is sent to the back

parts.note: x is the algebraic unknown
P is the abbreviation for page
articles are items or things

explanation.surface: Mysterious tiny particles written about on a page, nature unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: these particles are hypothetical, known only on paper, while ARTICLES is placed on (after) P with X in front.
explanation.definitionFit: X-particles are hypothetical heavy subatomic bosons proposed in grand unified theories, existing so far only in theory.

clue.text: See 24
Bat Richards and a bowler (old) in test

parts.note: Viv Richards, the great West Indies batsman
the a, joined on
Bill Voce, England fast bowler of the 1930s Bodyline series

explanation.surface: A batsman and a veteran bowler line up in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' suggests a cricket Test match, but here it is an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an oral examination, especially for a university degree.

clue.text: The steel menagerie has Woody hid

indicators.note: 'has' says the phrase holds something within it
'hid' confirms the thing held is concealed inside the phrase

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A metal zoo is hiding someone called Woody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has Woody hid' wraps around the definition: the phrase has the woody word hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmen is an old adjective meaning made of elm wood, hence woody.

clue.text: Round one: go round with general survey

parts.note: a round shape, the letter O

indicators.note: the second 'round' means surrounding, so that word encloses the one before it

parts.note: go in the sense of energy and dash
Roman numeral one
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A boxing commentator's broad survey after round one.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a broad summary of a subject, giving a general picture without detail.
